paper: step 8. Provisional Section 3.3. The commons reference evaluation model is a trained artifact.
adr: Diagnostic checkpoint sweep. Same corpus, taxonomy, gate, seed, and Qwen3 template as the 0.6B ceiling. Training base is Qwen3-1.7B: only the parameter count moves. This run does not decide the published pin; it samples the loss curve so a sweet spot or a capacity ceiling is a measured fact. The live pin is unchanged. After each checkpoint is merged, converted to GGUF Q8_0, and gated, the merged bf16 directory and that GGUF are deleted. Optimizer states are not kept on interval saves.

base.note: Read at run time from the manifest. repoId here is a pin that must match. This is the training base. Do not change the live evaluator pin in this diagnostic.

framework.whyNotUnsloth: 1.7B plus 3936 short examples on an 80GB card does not need Unsloth's memory path. The standard stack is the one a reader can follow without a third training runtime.
framework.torch: supplied by the GPU image; not pinned here so a CUDA wheel is not overwritten

train.evalDatasetNote: The held-out suite is the final gate, never a training or hyperparameter split. The sweep gates after the fact. It does not train against the suite.

sweep.purpose: Within-family capacity A/B versus the measured 0.6B ceiling. Same accepted sft.jsonl, same seed, same 187-item gate, same half-epoch interval, Qwen3 template with generation spans. Only the base moves from Qwen3-0.6B to Qwen3-1.7B. One GPU run, many gated checkpoints. Not a second gate, not a label change, not a live-pin swap.
sweep.diskHygieneNote: At start, delete stale merged dirs and GGUFs under the artifacts tree. Interval saves are adapter-only (no optimizer states) and capped at minCheckpoints. After each checkpoint is merged, converted Q8_0, and gated, delete the merged bf16 directory and that GGUF before the next checkpoint. Keep the LoRA adapter and the gate report.

llamaCpp.note: convert_hf_to_gguf.py then llama-quantize Q8_0. The run records the resolved commit in checkpoints.json.

time.estimate: Training three epochs of 1.7B LoRA is tens of minutes on an 80GB card. Six merge-plus-Q8_0 exports of 1.7B and six 187-item CPU gates dominate the wall time. Only one merged copy and one GGUF exist at a time. If the train loop itself is still running after 90 minutes, stop and report.
